one_liner: Research re-implementations of FST, CoCo-trie and MARISA succinct tries; C2-FST and C2-MARISA beat the originals on lookup and size.
what_it_does: Provides three static string-dictionary tries (c2::FstCC, CoCoCC, MarisaCC in include/fst_cc.hpp, coco_cc.hpp, marisa_cc.hpp) that map each key of a sorted or unsorted key set to a uint32_t id, with lookup returning -1 on a miss; FstCC also has successor, contains_prefix and range iteration. The interface is a template over the key type with build(begin, end, sorted, max_recursion, mask), not a drop-in for the marisa::Trie, SuRF or CoCo-trie APIs. The repo is mainly a paper artifact: benchmark.cpp with case IDs 0-14 and run_*.sh scripts reproduce the paper's tables against vendored baselines.
how_it_is_fast: The LOUDS-style topology and label bitvectors use a cache-conscious block layout: each 256-bit block keeps its absolute 32-bit rank, four 8-bit sub-ranks and the 256 bits together (c2::BitVector::Block, louds_cc.hpp), so rank, select and child navigation usually touch one block instead of separate rank/select directories. Adaptive unary-path compression keeps short terminal suffixes inline (at most 4 labels for FST, 3 for MARISA) and moves longer ones to a string pool that is either a recursive nested trie (depth rho 0-2) or an FSST or Re-pair tail container, chosen by size (strpool_t::build_optimal). rho=0 is the latency-optimal setting.
when_to_use: Static, build-once in-memory dictionaries of up to a few million strings (URLs, words, titles, domains) where both size and exact-lookup latency matter and MARISA or SuRF's FST is the incumbent.
C2-MARISA when you want a smaller-than-MARISA trie that is also faster: the independent 1M-key rerun has it 1.21-1.48x faster than MARISA on all 12 corpora.
C2-FST when you need ordered operations (successor, prefix test, range scan) on a compact trie and can test them on your own data first.
x86-64 Linux builds with GCC 10+ or Clang 12+, C++20 and Boost, where pulling in sdsl-lite, ds2i, sux and FSST as submodules is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: As a CoCo-trie replacement: in the independent rerun C2-CoCo was slower than upstream CoCo-trie on 7 of 8 corpora (0.78-0.92x) and larger on dna (10.25 vs 6.14 B/key); the README's 1.22x is against CoCo', the authors' own build with the original CoCo bitvector.
Persistent or memory-mapped dictionaries: the trie classes have no save/load or mmap path, so the structure must be rebuilt from the keys at every start.
Numeric-string corpora or very large key sets: the C2 variants produced no result on the numeric corpus in the rerun, and ids, ranks and positions are 32-bit (uint32_t) throughout.
Production code that needs maintenance: one public commit (2026-06-20), 0 stars, forked from HardyZ1906/C2, no issues, tests or releases.
Keys containing the 0x00 byte (it is the trie terminator label, c2::terminator_ = 0) or keys longer than 65535 bytes in C2-FST.

integration.form: header-only templates, but they include and link compiled third-party code (sdsl-lite, ds2i succinct, FSST static library); in practice a source-drop of include/ plus lib/
integration.dependencies: Boost (>= 1.71), sdsl-lite (vgteam fork), ds2i (aboffa fork), sux, FSST, and MARISA's grimoire vector header; all but Boost are git submodules included by relative paths like ../lib/ds2i/
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux tested; built with -march=native; GCC builtins (popcount, ctz, clz) are portable but other platforms are not documented
integration.thread_safety: not documented; lookups are const member functions on an immutable built structure, so concurrent reads look safe, but build is single-threaded and not reentrant

gotchas: C2-FST lookup stores the key length in a uint16_t (fst_cc.hpp: uint16_t len = key.size()), so keys of 65536 bytes or more are silently truncated and can match the wrong entry; MarisaCC uses uint32_t.

FstCC::successor returns the leaf id as soon as the query reaches a linked (pool-compressed) leaf, with the comment 'link: treat as exact match', without comparing the stored suffix; a query that diverges inside a compressed suffix can get a wrong successor. Seen in code, not tested here; the paper's headline numbers are exact lookups only.

FstCC, MarisaCC and CoCoCC own the suffix pool through a raw next_ pointer deleted in the destructor but keep implicit copy constructors, so copying a trie double-frees; calling build twice leaks the old pool, and BitVector grows with an unchecked realloc. Release builds compile asserts out, so an empty key set (assert(!key_set.empty())) is undefined behaviour.

benchmark.cpp prints [PASSED] unconditionally: lookup results are checked only when __CORRECTNESS_TEST__ is defined, which the CMake build does not set, and timed queries are shuffled existing keys only (no negative lookups). CMakeLists adds -w globally, so the advertised -Wall -pedantic warnings never show.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose C2-MARISA or C2-FST over MARISA, and over xcdat or Darts-clone, when you want a succinct trie with ordered or prefix queries that is both smaller and faster than MARISA or SuRF and you can rebuild it in memory at start-up; xcdat (2.2-2.9x faster than marisa on its Wiki set) and Darts-clone are the older, more widely used options, and lexindex was the smallest structure on all 13 corpora in the same campaign.
verified_claims_summary: Authors (README and arXiv 2606.16104, a single Intel Xeon Gold core with 25 MB LLC, model not stated) report up to 1.92x faster and 41% smaller for C2-FST against SuRF's FST, and up to 1.51x and 46% for C2-MARISA. The independent ilgrad/string-index-benchmarks rerun (GCC 16.2.1, -O3 -march=native, AMD Ryzen 7 5800HS, 1M keys, rho=0, timed with C2's own benchmark.cpp driver over positive lookups) has C2-MARISA 1.21-1.48x faster than MARISA on all 12 corpora and C2-FST 1.05-1.82x faster than FST on 11 of 12; that harness's author also maintains the competing lexindex.
status_note: Single-commit MIT-licensed paper artifact from 2026-06-20 with vendored baselines under their own licenses; worth vendoring include/ for an experiment, but expect to add serialization, copy semantics and tests before production use.
